svg.title: A request's lifecycle in the paged serving scheduler
svg.desc: A waiting request is admitted when its full current token history fits the KV reservation policy. It enters prefilling and advances its cached-token cursor until all current input tokens are cached. The final prefill produces the first output token for a new request. Running requests append the previous sampled token to KV, then sample the next one. EOS or the output budget finishes the request and releases its active KV references. Memory pressure can preempt a prefilling or running request: release active references, reset the cached cursor, preserve token history and request-local RNG, and return the request to the front of the waiting queue. Readmission may reuse warm prefix pages but otherwise recomputes missing history. The policy does not guarantee fairness or bounded latency.
svg.text: One request: admission, cached history, output, and cleanup
Paged-KV path; the state names describe eligibility for work, not four separate GPU queues.
admit
history cached;
sample next token
EOS or
output budget
WAITING
token history retained
no active KV ownership
wait for admission capacity
PREFILLING
KV space reserved
cache missing input tokens
partial chunks stay in this state
RUNNING
cache the last sampled token
sample the next output token
repeat until EOS or output limit
FINISHED
terminal bookkeeping
release active KV refs
remove from active work
Memory pressure: preempt a PREFILLING or RUNNING request back to WAITING.
Release its active KV refs; reset the cache cursor; keep token history and request-local RNG.
Admission reserves the current history
Reserve space for all current tokens, not just the next chunk.
A readmitted request includes its already generated tokens.
Reuse matching complete prefix blocks when available;
compute the missing history before sampling again.
Reservation does not prevent a later memory-pressure preemption.
The newest sampled token is not cached yet
final prefill: KV = [p0 p1 p2 p3 p4] → sample A1
next decode: KV = [p0 p1 p2 p3 p4 A1] → sample A2
Sampling adds a token to the request's history.
The next model call writes that token's K and V.
A's five-token prompt produces A1 at the end of its final prefill.
The first sampled token can immediately satisfy EOS or the output budget: RUNNING need not run a decode call.
Cancellation also performs terminal cleanup. Zero-output requests can finish without entering model execution.
Released pages can remain warm in the prefix cache. Releasing ownership is not the same as erasing their bytes.
This policy readmits preempted requests at the waiting-queue front; FCFS order alone does not guarantee fairness or bounded latency.
